ca_pump_rocks.blurb: Pump Rocks is a single freestanding boulder beside Highway 108, a little below 6,000 feet, in the Sonora Pass bouldering group. It holds nine problems with a flat landing at the base. The spread is wide for one rock: a few easy-to-moderate lines around V1 to V3, a pair at V4, and then a steep step up to V6, V7 and one V8. It makes a quick stop for someone driving over the pass with a pad, though it is not a destination for a full day of climbing.

ca_rusty_nail_area.blurb: Rusty Nail Area is the dark wall just beyond Heart Rock, one of the compact cliffs of New Directions north of Kernville in the southern Sierra. It has nine routes, five sport and four trad, with grades running from 5.9 up to 5.12. Some lines are two pitches. The climbing is steep slab, with older-style ratings, on clean rock that picks up good sun when the weather cools. The cliffs around it work best from fall through spring and run hot in summer. A friction slab sits below the right side of the wall.

ca_cookie_sheet_the.blurb: The Cookie Sheet is a big granite slab on the slope above and east of Cookie Cliff, in the Lower Merced River Canyon of Yosemite. It has nine routes, seven trad and two sport, mostly between 5.7 and 5.9. Most are multi-pitch, commonly three or four pitches, with some pitches long enough that two 60 m ropes help for the rappels. The slab is polished in places, and one route on the far left is a bolted line that suits a top-rope warm-up. It sees few climbers and works well for moderate days down canyon.

ca_last_temptation_cliff.blurb: Last Temptation Cliff is a small sandstone crag in the Castle Rock area of the Santa Cruz Mountains, passed on the trail toward Goat Rock. It has nine routes: four sport, four trad and one top-rope. The grades lean hard for a crag this size, with five climbs at 5.11, two at 5.10 and a couple of easier trad lines at 5.8 and 5.9. Most routes have anchors on top, and a walk-off trail runs down the left side of the cliff, so it suits a short session between bigger walls.

ca_sidewinder.blurb: Sidewinder is a short south-facing wall on the ridge that separates the Middle Earth valley from the Vader area, on Fairview Mountain near Apple Valley. It has nine routes: eight sport and one top-rope offwidth. Grades run from 5.7 through 5.12, with a cluster around 5.10, so it offers something for a mixed party. The wall is small and looks out over Middle Earth. Several of the lines carry snake names.
ca_sidewinder.approach: Follow the main trail up, swing around the left side of the Tatooine area, then pass between the Vader roof and the Twin Towers. The wall is right there on the ridge.

ca_skyline_boulder.blurb: Skyline Boulder is a lone, tall boulder in the Snow Summit group above Big Bear Lake in the San Bernardino Mountains, at roughly 8,000 feet. It faces south and is covered in knobs, which carry most of the climbing. There are nine problems, all in the beginner to lower-moderate range: six at VB or V0, two at V1 and one V2. Some knobs have broken off, so choose the solidly set ones, and a spotter is useful on a few lines. The way down is an easy downclimb off the back.
ca_skyline_boulder.approach: A level trail of roughly 70 meters leads to the boulder from the road; the walk takes about a minute.

ca_shooting_gallery_the.blurb: The Shooting Gallery is a very small crag in Jacoby Canyon, north of Big Bear City in the San Bernardino Mountains, at about 7,200 feet. The climbs are short and steep, on boulder-sized mini-crags in a streambed. It has nine routes: four sport, four top-rope and one trad. Most sit around 5.10, with a pair at 5.11 and a single easier line near 5.7, so it suits a short session rather than a full day. A second small crag lies a little farther down the canyon.
ca_shooting_gallery_the.approach: Walk about 150 yards along the streambed from where you park. It is the first of the two small crags in the canyon, and the bolts show on the boulder-sized rocks.
